title: NY State Assembly · District 80
area: The Bronx: Allerton, Morris Park, Norwood, Pelham Gardens, Pelham Parkway, and Van Nest

context.text: Both parties' primaries scheduled for June 23, 2026 were canceled. Incumbent John Zaccaro Jr. (D) advanced without appearing on the ballot. Denise Smith withdrew from the Republican primary but advanced from the Conservative Party primary without appearing on the ballot, so she appears on the Conservative Party line only.

priorities.text: "In just three years, he has helped secure millions in funding and advance legislation that strengthens neighborhoods across the district," with investments listed in schools and youth programs, housing stability and senior services, community safety and mental health resources, and parks and local business corridors.

Looking ahead, his stated priorities include expanding after-school programs and school-to-career pathways, protecting Mitchell-Lama housing and supporting homeowners and tenants, investing in community-based public-safety and mental-health services, expanding senior services, and improving city and state agency responsiveness.

He announced that the 2024 state budget included new enforcement powers to revoke the tobacco, liquor, or lottery licenses of businesses that possess or sell illegal cannabis, which he described as a win against illegal smoke shops in his district.

record.text: Announced that the state budget signed in April 2024 gave localities new enforcement powers to revoke tobacco, liquor, or lottery licenses from businesses selling illegal cannabis, targeting unlicensed smoke shops in his district.
As of the 2025-2026 session, serves on the Assembly's Aging, Alcoholism and Drug Abuse, Economic Development/Job Creation/Commerce and Industry, Education, Housing, and Small Business committees.

candidates.name: Denise Smith

priorities.text: Senior care and nursing home oversight, including quality of care, stronger oversight, and auditing how funds are used, as described in Bronx.com coverage of her remarks to the Bronx Conservative Party.
Public safety, foster care reform, and transit issues, as described in the same Bronx.com coverage.

candidates.researchNotes: No Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey response, campaign website, or news coverage of policy positions could be located for Smith as of September 25, 2026. Her Ballotpedia page lists only personal and 2025 campaign social-media accounts (Facebook, Instagram, TikTok), which were inaccessible or contained no public posts on the current race. Re-checked 2026-10-19: Bronx.com's report of her January 2026 remarks to the Bronx Conservative Party contains no direct quotes from her, so no statements or positions were added; priorities are the reporter's summary.

researchNotes: Zaccaro has not completed Ballotpedia's Candidate Connection survey in any election cycle (2026, 2024, or 2022); his priorities are documented from his own campaign website's Record & Priorities and About pages, which list general goals (defending Mitchell-Lama housing, expanding after-school programs, community-based safety) without a stated stance matching any of this guide's 15 fixed issue keys, so no Position entries are included. Smith has no campaign website found and has not completed Ballotpedia's Candidate Connection survey, so her entry is marked 'minimal.' No public biography (birthplace, education, or career) was found for Smith beyond her 2025 and 2026 candidacies.
